paper.title: Outcomes After Intervention in Radiation-Induced Carotid Artery Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

source.text:
Outcomes After Intervention in Radiation-Induced Carotid Artery Stenosis: A 
Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

BACKGROUND: To assess clinical outcomes after carotid endarterectomy (CEA), 
transfemoral carotid artery stenting (CAS), and transcarotid artery 
revascularization in patients with radiation-induced carotid artery stenosis 
(RICS) utilizing a systematic review and meta-analysis.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the literature was performed. 
We focused on 30-day and long-term outcomes. Study quality was assessed using 
the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.
RESULTS: Among 36 study-arms (32 publications, 6,695 patients), the pooled 
30-day stroke rate was 1.93% (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.36-2.74%) and 
30-day composite outcome rate was 2.75% (95% CI 1.89-3.99%). Restenosis occurred 
in 10.51% (95% CI 7.61-14.33%) and reintervention in 6.53% (95% CI 4.29-9.83%) 
of patients. Subgroup analysis showed numerically higher restenosis (12.0% vs. 
5.98%; P = 0.05) and significantly higher reintervention rates (8.06% vs. 2.21%; 
P = 0.004) after CAS than CEA. In the comparative analysis against nonirradiated 
controls, perioperative outcomes were similar between groups; however, 
restenosis (odds ratio [OR] 3.13, 95% CI 1.24-7.89; P = 0.028) and 
reintervention rates (OR 3.86, 95% CI 1.13-13.17; P = 0.022) were significantly 
higher in RICS patients. Time from radiotherapy to revascularization was not 
associated with restenosis or reintervention rates (P = 0.46 and P = 0.34, 
respectively).
CONCLUSION: Carotid revascularization in patients with RICS appears to be safe, 
with perioperative outcomes similar to those in nonirradiated patients. The main 
difference was in long-term follow-up, where restenosis and reintervention occur 
3-4 times more frequently than in atherosclerotic controls. CEA also showed 
better long-term durability than CAS. These findings support close long-term 
surveillance in this population.

round3DisplayedFinding: Revascularization in radiation-induced carotid stenosis appeared as safe perioperatively as in nonirradiated patients, but restenosis and reintervention were significantly more frequent over long-term follow-up, and stenting had higher reintervention rates than endarterectomy.
